related_resources.reason: Exact Riemann interface state used as a shared numerical flux.
Transonic entropy correction and why naive approximate fluxes can fail.
Conservative cell-average update and flux cancellation.

authorship.scope: Original foundation-first Burgers/Riemann/entropy, Godunov flux and MUSCL-limiter lectures and companions; preserve all 57 previous manuscripts and their individual metadata.

prerequisites.reason: Shows nonlinear shock formation, weak conservation, and the admissibility problem.
Derives shock/rarefaction Riemann solutions and the entropy test.
Builds conservative finite-volume balance laws and shared face-flux bookkeeping.

background: Elementary single-variable calculus and algebra; prior characteristics, upwind CFL and finite-volume balances; no advanced nonlinear shock stability or functional analysis assumed.
readiness_checks: Calculate Godunov fluxes for shocks of either propagation direction and a transonic fan.
Update four periodic cell averages and check total mass.
Explain why conservation and flux consistency are not sufficient entropy guarantees.

description: Constructs Godunov fluxes from local Riemann problems at cell boundaries, calculates a finite-volume update, and separates conservation from stability and entropy properties.
